event.title: Syrian Court Sentences Bashar al-Assad to Death in Absentia for War Crimes
event.canonical_title: Syrian Court Sentences Bashar al-Assad to Death in Absentia for War Crimes
event.summary: A Syrian court has sentenced former president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during the country's civil war. The ruling also included their cousin Atef Najib, who was present at the trial. The court's decision follows a lengthy conflict that has resulted in approximately half a million deaths.

timeline.title: Bashar al-Assad Sentenced to Death in Absentia for War Crimes
timeline.summary: A Syrian court has sentenced former president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia for war crimes and crimes against humanity related to the civil war. The court's decision comes after both men were found responsible for their actions in the conflict, which has resulted in approximately 500,000 deaths. The two brothers are currently believed to be in Moscow.

event_overview.title: About Syria Conflict
event_overview.subject: Syria Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Syria conflict began with anti-government protests in March 2011 and escalated into armed conflict involving Syrian state forces, opposition armed groups, extremist organizations and foreign actors. It has produced a major humanitarian and displacement crisis, while international efforts have combined diplomacy, humanitarian relief and mechanisms intended to support accountability for serious international crimes.

facts.label: Origin and location
facts.value: The conflict began in Syria in March 2011, after protests that started in Dar'a spread following the violent suppression of demonstrations.

facts.label: Political framework
facts.value: UN Security Council resolution 2254, adopted in 2015, remains the UN-backed framework cited for pursuing a Syrian-led, negotiated political settlement rather than a military solution.

facts.label: International accountability mechanism
facts.value: The UN General Assembly established the International, Impartial and Independent Mechanism (IIIM) on December 21, 2016, to assist investigations and prosecutions of those responsible for the most serious crimes under international law committed in Syria since March 2011.

facts.label: Legal scope
facts.value: The IIIM is not itself a court: it collects, consolidates, preserves and analyzes material and prepares case files for use by competent jurisdictions, subject to human-rights and fair-trial standards.

facts.label: Humanitarian and regional impact
facts.value: The conflict has displaced Syrians both within the country and across the region; UNHCR identifies Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon and Türkiye among the countries affected by the Syria emergency.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the specific reported court proceedings concerning Bashar al-Assad; it does not attempt to catalog the full military, political, humanitarian or accountability history of the Syria conflict.
